chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ataa, from Salam ibn Abi 'Umrah, who said:

Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: 'The master of this matter will have a house called the House of Praise. In it is a lamp that shines from the day he was born until he rises with the sword.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الأَمْرِ: The Master of the Matter (referring to the Imam/Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the House of Praise and its lamp in the description of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the metaphysical signs of the Mahdi (a.s.) through the 'Bait al-Hamd' (House of Praise), a dwelling containing a divine lamp that has shone continuously since his birth. This luminous sign symbolizes his hidden spiritual authority and will remain lit until his reappearance to establish global justice, reflecting the Shia belief in the continuity of divine guidance even during the Major Occultation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 483 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ja’far Himyari, from his father from Muhammad bin Isa from Muhammad bin Ataa from Salam bin Abi Umrah that he said:

Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) said: “The man of this matter will have a house called Baitul Hamd (house of praise). It will have a lamp, which was lighted since the day of his birth and it will continue to burn until the day he will rise with the sword.”
